pointers.sentence: That function calls `django.setup` and then returns a new `WSGIHandler` (`django/core/wsgi.py:get_wsgi_application`).

Each middleware's line names `MiddlewareMixin.__init__` because all seven are built on `MiddlewareMixin`, whose constructor runs when any of them is made (`django/middleware/__init__.py:MiddlewareMixin.__init__`).

Here the module is imported when `django.setup` reads its first setting, an argument for `configure_logging`, and the recording marks that moment with `LazySettings._setup` (`django/__init__.py:setup`).
`django.conf.settings` is a `LazySettings`, made when `django.conf` is imported and empty until its first use (`django/conf/__init__.py:settings`).
Without the variable, it raises `ImproperlyConfigured` (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings._setup`).

`Settings.__init__` copies every upper-case name of `django/conf/global_settings.py` onto itself, then imports the project's module and copies its upper-case names over them (`django/conf/__init__.py:Settings.__init__`).

Every value read through the proxy is then kept on the proxy itself (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings.__getattr__`).

The docstring of `LazySettings` names both: the user can configure the settings by hand before using them, and otherwise Django uses the module that `"DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE"` names (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings`).
Configuring by hand must come first: `LazySettings.configure` raises `RuntimeError` once the settings are loaded (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings.configure`).

It holds a lock, returns at once when it has already run, raises if it is entered again while running, and runs three phases over `settings.INSTALLED_APPS` in order (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.populate`).

`AppConfig.create` imports the entry's module and looks in its `apps` submodule, if it has one, for the `AppConfig` subclass to use; a dotted path to a configuration class is accepted too (`django/apps/config.py:AppConfig.create`).
An application's label is its key in `Apps.app_configs`, and a label taken twice makes `Apps.populate` raise `ImproperlyConfigured` (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.populate`).
`AppConfig.import_models` imports the application's `models` module if it has one (`django/apps/config.py:AppConfig.import_models`).

Importing it runs each model's class statement, where the metaclass, `ModelBase`, builds the class and its `_meta` and registers it if it is not abstract (`django/db/models/base.py:ModelBase.__new__`); [`ModelBase`: a class statement becomes a model](../models/metaclass.md) tells each step.
`Apps.register_model` files the class under its application label and lower-case name, the key `Apps.get_model` answers to (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.register_model`).

The through table a many-to-many field makes for itself, such as auth's Group_permissions, is a model made while its own model's fields are set up, so it is registered before the model that declares the field (`django/db/models/fields/related.py:ManyToManyField.contribute_to_class`).
`AppConfig.ready` is the hook for work that needs every model to exist (`django/apps/config.py:AppConfig.ready`).

In the admin, `AdminConfig.ready` calls `autodiscover`, which imports the `admin` module of every installed application so that their `ModelAdmin` registrations run (`django/contrib/admin/apps.py:AdminConfig.ready`, `django/utils/module_loading.py:autodiscover_modules`).

In the admin, `AdminConfig.ready` calls `autodiscover`, which imports the `admin` module of every installed application so that their `ModelAdmin` registrations run (`django/contrib/admin/apps.py:AdminConfig.ready`, `django/utils/module_loading.py:autodiscover_modules`).

A models module that calls `Apps.get_model` while it is being imported gets `AppRegistryNotReady`, `"Models aren't loaded yet."`, even for a model registered earlier in the same phase: by default the method answers only once the phase is over and `Apps.models_ready` is set (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.get_model`).
With the registry ready, `get_wsgi_application` returns a `WSGIHandler`, whose constructor ends by calling `BaseHandler.load_middleware` (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIHandler.__init__`).

So `SecurityMiddleware`, first in the setting and made last, is the outermost layer, and `XFrameOptionsMiddleware`, made first, the innermost (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.load_middleware`).

`SecurityMiddleware` reads settings into attributes when it is made and never reads them again, and `SessionMiddleware` imports the session engine that `settings.SESSION_ENGINE` names and keeps its session store class (`django/middleware/security.py:SecurityMiddleware.__init__`, `django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py:SessionMiddleware.__init__`).
